thread.title: Dow Drops 519 Points Because the Market Has Bigger Problems Than Just Apple - Barron's

title: Dow Drops 519 Points Because the Market Has Bigger Problems Than Just Apple - Barron's
text:
Dow Drops 660 Points Because the Market Has Bigger Problems Than Just Apple By Updated Jan. 3, 2019 4:07 p.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
If only we could just blame Apple (AAPL) for the Dow Jones Industrial Average’s 600-point tumble. But no—there is a lot more going on today.
The S&P 500 has dropped 2.5% to 2447.89, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has slumped 660.02 points, or 2.8%, to 22,686.22. The Nasdaq Composite has tumbled 3% to 6463.50.
And Apple is certainly a big part of that drop. Apple stock dropped 10% at $142.08 after its disappointing guidance , and as the market’s now fourth-biggest stock, it weighs on the indexes—and tech in particular. The S&P 500 Information Technology Sector Index has dropped 5.1%.
But the next two worst performing sectors are the S&P 500 Industrials Sector and the S&P 500 Materials Sector , off 3% and 2.8% respectively. And that tells us that concerns about slowing economic growth and a potential recession are weighing on the market.
And there is good reason for that. The Institute for Supply Management’s manufacturing index fell to 54.1 in December , its lowest reading since 2016 and well below predictions for 57.9. A reading over 50, however, still indicates economic growth. “It is clear that the growth slowdown overseas has now made it to our shores along with the interest rate sensitive areas of the U.S. economy that has already been affected,” writes Bleakley Advisory Group’s Peter Boockvar .
And then we had Dallas Fed President Robert Kapan calling for an end to the Fed’s rate increases , at least for the first half of the year, which doesn’t exactly inspire confidence in the state of the economy.
Add it all up, and we’re back where we were before Christmas—with the market falling, and falling hard.
